_note: Historical outbreaks used for context. Figures are as published by the cited sources; where sources differ, the range or the most authoritative figure is given. Re-verify figures against the sources before an official presentation. Projections scale published attack/hospitalisation/death rates to the affected population and are illustrative, not forecasts.

events.name: 2009 H1N1 influenza pandemic (United States)
events.deaths: 12,469 in the US (range 8,868-18,306); 151,700-575,400 worldwide in the first year
events.economic_impact: Mass vaccination campaign; school closures in several states.
events.social_impact: Deaths concentrated in working-age adults (about 9,570 of the US deaths were aged 18-64).
events.lessons: A novel virus first spread among young people and schools; surveillance and rapid vaccine production mattered.

sources.title: CDC estimates of 2009 H1N1 influenza cases, hospitalizations and deaths

events.name: COVID-19 pandemic
events.cases: Hundreds of millions of reported infections
events.deaths: About 14.9 million excess deaths in 2020-2021 (range 13.3-16.6 million, WHO)
events.hospitalisations: Health systems in many countries exceeded intensive-care capacity
events.economic_impact: Global output fell by roughly 3% in 2020, the deepest contraction since the Great Depression (IMF World Economic Outlook).
events.social_impact: Prolonged school closures, lockdowns, disruption of routine care, long-term effects on learning and mental health.
events.lessons: Weeks of earlier detection of an unexplained pneumonia cluster, open data sharing and rapid testing change outcomes by orders of magnitude.

sources.title: WHO: 14.9 million excess deaths associated with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and 2021

events.name: SARS outbreak
events.location: 29 countries (largest in China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore, Canada)
events.hospitalisations: Most cases were hospitalised; many were health-care workers
events.economic_impact: Lee and McKibbin (2004) modelled large global losses concentrated in East Asia, driven by falls in travel, retail and confidence.
events.social_impact: Hospital outbreaks, quarantine of thousands of contacts in Toronto and Asia, travel advisories.
events.lessons: Early recognition of an unexplained severe pneumonia cluster and strict infection control in hospitals were decisive.

sources.title: Lee & McKibbin, Globalization and Disease: The Case of SARS (Brookings)

events.name: MERS outbreak, Republic of Korea
events.hospitalisations: All cases; transmission mainly inside hospitals
events.economic_impact: Tourism losses estimated at up to 3.4 trillion won (Korea Culture & Tourism Institute); the Bank of Korea cut its 2015 growth forecast from 3.1% to 2.8%; a 22 trillion won (about US$19.8 billion) stimulus package followed.
events.social_impact: Thousands quarantined; schools closed; a single imported case seeded the outbreak.
events.lessons: Delayed recognition in emergency departments allowed super-spreading; transparency about affected hospitals restored trust.

sources.title: Korea Times: tourism industry suffers 3.4 trillion won loss from MERS

events.name: 1918 influenza pandemic (H1N1)
events.cases: about 500 million infected (one third of the world's population)
events.economic_impact: Large but poorly measured; widespread closures of schools, theatres and businesses.
events.social_impact: High mortality among young adults; overwhelmed health systems.
events.lessons: Early, sustained non-pharmaceutical interventions were associated with lower peak mortality in US cities.

events.name: SARS cluster at Amoy Gardens housing estate, Hong Kong
events.economic_impact: Block E isolated and residents moved to quarantine camps.
events.social_impact: About one fifth of Hong Kong's 1,755 SARS cases came from this single estate.
events.lessons: A neighbourhood-level cluster can signal an environmental transmission route (here, faulty drainage) that needs engineering, not only clinical, investigation.

events.name: Cryptosporidium outbreak from the municipal water supply, Milwaukee
events.economic_impact: US$96.2 million in 1993 dollars: US$31.7 million medical costs and US$64.6 million lost productivity (Corso et al. 2003).
events.social_impact: Boil-water advisory for the whole city; the largest documented waterborne outbreak in US history.
events.lessons: Rises in pharmacy sales of anti-diarrhoeals and in GI visits across a wide area preceded official recognition.

sources.title: Corso et al., Costs of illness in the 1993 waterborne Cryptosporidium outbreak, Emerging Infectious Diseases 2003

events.population_note: Approximate population of the greater Milwaukee area served by the affected water utility; rates are approximate.

events.name: E. coli O104:H4 outbreak, Germany
events.hospitalisations: about 850 cases of haemolytic uraemic syndrome
events.economic_impact: Severe losses for vegetable growers after early public warnings about cucumbers, tomatoes and lettuce; the vehicle was fenugreek sprouts.
events.social_impact: Adults, especially women, were most affected; dialysis capacity strained.
events.lessons: Fast, accurate source attribution matters: premature attribution caused large economic damage to the wrong sector.

sources.title: Robert Koch Institute: Final presentation and evaluation of the EHEC O104:H4/HUS outbreak

events.name: Legionnaires' disease outbreak, South Bronx, New York City
events.location: South Bronx, New York City, USA
events.cases: 128 (as of the end of the outbreak, 20 August 2015)
events.economic_impact: Emergency disinfection of cooling towers city-wide; new registration and inspection requirements for cooling towers in New York City and State.
events.social_impact: Concentrated in a low-income neighbourhood; strong public concern and political scrutiny.
events.lessons: Spatial clustering of pneumonia among older adults should trigger an environmental search for aerosol sources within days.

sources.title: NY1: Health commissioner says Legionnaires' outbreak in South Bronx is over

events.name: Measles epidemic, Samoa
events.economic_impact: State of emergency; government services and businesses closed for mass vaccination days.
events.social_impact: Schools and the university closed; vaccination coverage raised from about 31% to about 94% of the eligible population in weeks.
events.lessons: Low childhood vaccination coverage turns a single introduction into a national emergency.

sources.title: 2019 Samoa measles outbreak (summary with primary references)

events.name: Norovirus: annual global burden
events.economic_impact: US$4.2 billion direct health-system costs and US$60.3 billion societal costs per year; children under 5 account for about US$39.8 billion (Bartsch et al. 2016).
events.social_impact: School and care-home outbreaks cause closures and staff absence.
events.lessons: School outbreaks are usually short; rapid exclusion of ill pupils and staff for 48 hours after symptoms and chlorine cleaning shorten them.

sources.title: Bartsch et al., Global economic burden of norovirus gastroenteritis, PLoS ONE 2016

events.name: Ebola virus disease epidemic, West Africa
events.hospitalisations: Health systems collapsed in the three most affected countries
events.economic_impact: Total economic and social burden estimated at US$53.19 billion, including deaths from other diseases due to disrupted care (Huber et al. 2018).
events.social_impact: Schools closed for months; routine immunisation and maternal care disrupted.
events.lessons: Indirect deaths from disrupted health services can exceed direct deaths; early community engagement is essential.

sources.title: Huber, Finelli & Stevens, The economic and social burden of the 2014 Ebola outbreak in West Africa, J Infect Dis 2018
